cards.back: Light in fiber covers about 200 km per millisecond. Chennai to Virginia is about 230 ms per round trip, and a secure connection takes two or three round trips before any work.
Serves users from a nearby server 5 to 20 ms away. On a miss it fetches from your origin over a warm connection and caches the file for the next user.
A small CDN site in a city: a few racks of cache servers and routers, usually in a shared data center.
Every PoP announces the same IP and BGP carries packets to the nearest one. A failed PoP stops announcing, and DDoS traffic spreads across all PoPs.
An internet exchange point is a building where networks plug into a shared switch and exchange traffic directly, usually free (peering), instead of paying transit.
Its peering: short, cheap paths into each ISP. Huge video volumes are affordable only because they're served from caches inside or next to the user's ISP.
A mid-tier cache between PoPs and origin, so a new file causes one origin request per shield instead of one per PoP. It also collapses simultaneous requests.
Files like app.3f9a1c.js never change, so cache them for a year with max-age=31536000, immutable, and deploy new names instead of purging.
Leave out query parameters that don't change the response, like utm_source, and use Vary only for headers that really matter, or the hit ratio collapses.
Serve the old copy while fetching a new one, and keep serving it if the origin is down.
The expensive handshake happens near the user instead of across the world, which speeds up even uncacheable API calls.

quiz.q: The CDN hit ratio suddenly drops and origin load jumps 10×. What should you check first?
choices: The cache key: random query strings, cookies or Vary: User-Agent
quiz.why: A bad cache key splits one file into thousands of entries; fix it before scaling the origin.

quiz.q: A user's account page got served to other users from the CDN. What went wrong?
choices: A personal response was cached under a shared key
Anycast routed to the wrong PoP
quiz.why: Mark personal responses private and test with two accounts.

quiz.q: A new release asset is requested from 300 PoPs at once and the origin struggles. What helps?
choices: An origin shield that collapses misses
quiz.why: PoPs ask the shield, and only the shield asks the origin.

quiz.q: How should you ship a changed JavaScript bundle without purging?
choices: Deploy it under a new content-hashed file name
quiz.why: Versioned names mean nothing needs purging, and the old file can stay cached.

quiz.q: You purge the entire CDN before a launch and the origin falls over. Why?
choices: Full load hit an origin sized for about 10% of it
quiz.why: Purge by tag, warm caches for big launches, and keep the shield on.

quiz.q: An API's responses can't be cached. Can a CDN still make it faster?
choices: No, CDNs only help static files
Yes, TLS terminates at the edge near the user
quiz.why: The handshake happens 8 ms away instead of 230 ms, and the PoP keeps a warm connection to the origin.
